<jats:p>
                    Let
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>𝒪</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    be a compact Riemannian orbisurface. We compute formulas for the contribution of cone points of 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>𝒪</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    to the coefficient at 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msup>
                        <mml:mi>t</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                      </mml:msup>
                    </mml:math>
                    of the asymptotic expansion of the heat trace of 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>𝒪</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    , the contributions at
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msup>
                        <mml:mi>t</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mn>0</mml:mn>
                      </mml:msup>
                    </mml:math>
                    and
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msup>
                        <mml:mi>t</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                      </mml:msup>
                    </mml:math>
                    being known from the literature. As an application, we compute the coefficient at 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msup>
                        <mml:mi>t</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                      </mml:msup>
                    </mml:math>
                    of the contribution of interior angles of the form
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>γ</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>π</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>/</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>k</mml:mi>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    in geodesic polygons in surfaces to the asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet heat kernel of the polygon, under a certain symmetry assumption locally near the corresponding corner. The main novelty here is the determination of the way in which the Laplacian of the Gauss curvature at the corner point enters into the coefficient at 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msup>
                        <mml:mi>t</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                      </mml:msup>
                    </mml:math>
                    . We finish with a conjecture concerning the analogous contribution of an arbitrary angle 
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>γ</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    in a geodesic polygon.
                  </jats:p>
title: On the corner contributions to the heat coefficients of geodesic polygons
